author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Written October 2, 1977 to Eugene Warren shortly after the Metz science-fiction festival, this letter reads Star Wars as Christian myth made literal, the old redemption story surfacing intact inside a mass-market space adventure.
page_summary:
In this October 1977 letter to Eugene Warren, a correspondent with whom PKD discussed religion and the Holy Spirit, Dick gives Star Wars a startlingly serious theological reading. He treats George Lucas's film not as light entertainment but as Christian myth breaking back through into popular culture, the archetypal story of redemption and cosmic conflict made vivid and literal for a mass audience.

The letter dates from the period just after PKD's celebrated appearance at the Metz festival in France, when his own thinking about 2-3-74 was turning toward the idea that ancient sacred patterns could erupt into the present. He read the slotted-eyed menace and blazing light of the film through the same imagery he used for his visions.

The letter is a compact instance of PKD's late habit of finding revealed religion hidden inside science fiction, and of taking that discovery in deadly earnest.
